D1.rationale: There is nothing to score. The fixture ships no cases, no adapters, no providers, no tests and no seeded behavioral faults -- only a model, a declared partition, a map, three code modules and the recorded refusal. Both ex6 runs are explicitly mechanical with no agent. Zero is the floor of the scale and it is where a fixture with no detection instrument sits; it is not a criticism of a fixture built to test a refusal.

D2.rationale: Complexity is measured and reported (descriptor-emergent.txt and descriptor-declared.txt ship with the fixture; I re-measured at scoring time: bound 1,344, Q = 0.000, one emergent component, four dense rows -- dirty 5/5, lastCommand 5/5, auditLog 4/5, status 4/5 -- and Q = -0.1856 with crossing fraction 0.8 under the declared partition), and the fixture argues the relationship between those figures and its design ('Every action below writes all four variables. That is the fixture'). Anchor 2 is definitionally unreachable: this is a god-state model where every variable is written from everywhere, on purpose. So the highest anchor fully satisfied is 1.

D3.rationale: Boundaries are named in a declaration (orders owns status, billing the audit trail, notify the flags) and the code does not follow them: every module reaches both others, billing reads orders' class dictionary by reflection (audit.py:19-22), and notify coordinates by polling both collaborators and re-stamping (flags.py:15-23). Anchor 1, which is the correct and intended outcome for a deliberately incoherent control. Not 2: there is no port anywhere in the code. Not 0 only because the declaration exists and each class does own its own field, so a boundary is at least discernible on paper. Note for the reader: the reflexion check reports ZERO divergences here, and that is not a modularity signal -- every component pair is ported because every action writes every variable, which is exactly why the verdict is unmappable.

D4.rationale: No baseline, no suite, no refactor, no behavior check of any kind exists in the fixture or in either run. Nothing was changed and nothing was checked, so there is no preservation to score. Zero is structural here rather than a defect finding, and the dimension should be read as not-applicable-scored-at-floor. One drift worth recording, not scored: the fixture's committed evidence/reflexion.txt predates the round-2 verdict rule and lacks the partition-decomposition block the tool prints today, so the shipped evidence file no longer matches the tool's output even though the verdict is unchanged.

D5.rationale: I reproduced the refusal today, independently: architecture_scan = unmappable, exit 0, with unfalsifiable_coherence AND partition_does_not_decompose as basis limits, 'a clean result is NOT SUPPORTABLE on this basis', and the sentence that no flag, key, annotation or environment variable turns it into coherent. That is anchor 3 in the program, not in prose. Anchor 2: the fixture's own README states the scoring rule that reporting 0 divergences as clean is a FAIL, and that 'fixing' it by declaring an escaping partition is also a FAIL. Anchor 4: the record is full of results unflattering to itself and to the epic -- the README argues at length that this synthetic fixture is WORSE evidence than the repository's own model and labels itself the control; it files a finding against the very mechanism it exists to demonstrate (consumable_as_architecture is true for any declared partition, so the criteria table does not stand between a project and a false clean); and run 1 scored the epic's own prediction MISSED, with the measured asymmetry that converted the headline refusal into a clean. A fixture whose own README explains why it is second-rate evidence is the artifact this dimension is for.
D5.refuses_to_claim: It refuses to call 0 divergences a clean result, refuses to present its 7 convergences as evidence the code respects a boundary, refuses to claim primacy over the real incoherent model in this repository, and refuses to claim that unfalsifiable_coherence catches anything beyond the degenerate case.

verdict: A control that does exactly one thing and does it honestly: the refusal reproduces on demand with two basis limits, and the fixture argues against its own importance while filing a finding against the mechanism it exists to prove -- with no detection instrument, no behavior check and, by construction, no modularity.
